title: Daybench notebook: 4-bit quant + KV cache quick experiments
content:
Quick notes (daybench) — goal: micro-evaluate 4-bit quantization + KV/prefix caching behavior on chat-style flows and capture failure modes. Short, messy log for myself.

Date & context:
- 2026-03-28 -> baseline runs. 2026-04-02 -> followups with small fixes to batching policy.
- Hardware: r4g-16 (A100-like) dev pool. Using latest runtime branch: runtimes/quant-optim-2026-03 (local build).

Experiment high-level objective:
- Can we reliably use 4-bit quant (q4_0 style) for our small-medium models in hosted/dedicated while keeping p95 latency under 150ms at short sequences (<=128) for chat prefix cases?
- Understand KV-cache warm vs cold behaviors: prefix caching should kick in after first message; measure cost of cache miss vs hit.

Setup (scripts + config snippets):
- model: rw-small-v1 (baseline float32), rw-small-v1-q4 (q4_0), rw-small-v1-q8 (fake-int8 fallback)
- seq: 64, 128, 256 (mostly focusing 128)
- batch sizes: 1, 2, 4 (continuous batching enabled)
- caching: prefix_cache=true, kv_cache_ttl=300s, cache_shard=2
- metrics captured: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec, GPU memory, decode-fail count, repetition score (cheap heuristic)
- code: /home/isla/daybench/run.sh -> calls microbench harness that hits the health-check + chat endpoints with chat-history length param

Runs (raw lines from harness):
- RUN A (baseline float32) seq=128 batch=1 prefix_cold -> p95=98ms, tok/s=1850, GPU mem=7.6GB
- RUN B (q8 fallback) seq=128 batch=1 prefix_cold -> p95=110ms, tok/s=1950, GPU mem=5.1GB
- RUN C (q4_0) seq=128 batch=1 prefix_cold -> p95=158ms, tok/s=2300, GPU mem=3.2GB (occasional decode smoothing hiccup)
- RUN D (q4_0) seq=128 batch=1 prefix_warm -> p95=132ms, tok/s=2350, GPU mem=3.2GB
- RUN E (q4_0) seq=64 batch=2 prefix_warm -> p95=98ms, tok/s=3100, GPU mem=3.4GB

Tabular quick view (human-readable):
Model | Quant | Seq | Batch | prefix | p95 ms | tok/s | GPU mem
rw-small-v1 | fp32 | 128 | 1 | cold | 98 | 1850 | 7.6GB
rw-small-v1 | q8 | 128 | 1 | cold | 110 | 1950 | 5.1GB
rw-small-v1 | q4_0 | 128 | 1 | cold | 158 | 2300 | 3.2GB
rw-small-v1 | q4_0 | 128 | 1 | warm | 132 | 2350 | 3.2GB
rw-small-v1 | q4_0 | 64 | 2 | warm | 98 | 3100 | 3.4GB

Observations / interpretations (quick):
- q4 gives big throughput wins and memory savings but increases p95 on cold prefix path; warm cache helps but not fully back to fp32 baseline at same batch.
- Batching + short sequences (seq=64, batch=2) recovers latency and gives excellent tokens/sec; ideal for burst-y PLG endpoints.
- Decoding quality: small number of hallucinations / repetition spikes in q4_0 runs. Need to quantify with eval set (not just heuristic).
- Runtime kernel selection: fallback to slower kernel on first block for q4 conversion appears to cost ~20–30ms (investigate where).

Failure modes seen:
- Rare decode crash when long token IDs > 1024 after many prefixes (repro 1/200). Stack suggests KV pointer overflow in quantized path. Filed repro in linked PR.
- Cache invalidation race when client sends a rapid edit -> double insert into cache shard causes slight latency spike (race window ~8–12ms but increases p95).

Immediate next steps / TODO (short):
- [ ] Run formal eval on 200 curated prompts (fidelity + repetition) across fp32/q8/q4_0 and capture BLEU-ish + repetition metrics. (owner: me)
- [ ] Add microprofiling to runtime to timestamp kernel pick + conversion timing; correlate with p95 jumps (owner: Rajesh) -> link to PR 4123.
- [ ] Re-run cold-start stress (simulate 50 concurrent new sessions) and capture percentiles up to p999. (owner: Marta)
- [ ] Add quick A/B config in dev console for canary: q4_0 with prefix_cache on, roll 5% (need product ok).
- [ ] Triage KV overflow bug; create minimal reproducer and add fuzz test to runtime.

Scratch code / commands (for myself):
- run harness: ./daybench/run.sh --model rw-small-v1-q4 --seq 128 --batch 1 --prefix cold --iters 500
- quick profiler: python tools/kv_prof.py --trace 10 --out /tmp/kv-trace.json
- repro crash: ./repro/kv-overflow --seed 42 --len 1200

Open questions / hypotheses to test:
- Is the cold-start kernel conversion overhead linear with sequence length or constant per-init? I think it's ~constant per request for first block; need micro timestamps.
- How much of the latency gap is due to quantized matmul vs additional memory indirections introduced by q4 packing?
- Can we safely use q4 for Dedicated (reserved) tiers where warm cache is likely? If yes, craft guidance: q4+prefix=true recommended for dedicated; hosted needs fallback rules.

Notes to self (random):
- If we can shave ~20ms from conversion overhead, q4 becomes default for small models for dedicated customers.
- Ask infra about pre-warming shards for heavy PLG days (weekend runs).
- Keep this as a short living doc; copy results into a formal bench doc if numbers stabilize.

End of notebook snapshot.

-- Isla
